rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Objective 2 Gameplay 3 End of the Game 4 Options Objective Play cards to change rules and collect keepers, then set a goal for you to win! Just beware: this party game is nearly chaos! Gameplay Place the basic rules (draw 1, play 1) and deal 3 cards to each player. On your turn, draw and play cards as required. If the played card is a rule card, apply immediately and discard any contradicting rules. If it is a keeper card, you collect the keeper. If it is a goal card, replace the old goal with the new goal. If it is an action, apply it immediately then discard. After you play the cards required (and activate any extra actions), discard cards down to the hand and keeper limit. End of the Game The game ends if someone meets the condition of the current goal. That player wins immediately even if out of turn. If two or more players meet the winning condition, play until a single winner remains. Options Creeper Pack: 4 creepers are added to the game. When a creeper is drawn it is played immediately and another card is redrawn. When you have a creeper you cannot win unless a card said otherwise.

---

[Rating: 1/10] I hate this game. I've actually played a game with a drunk who was ABSENT FROM THE ROOM for most of the game - and he still won. It's that frakin' random.

[Rating: 1/10] No game here.  Boring game. Boring text.  Dull experience.  Can be quick if you're unlucky, or really long if you're really unlucky.  Lucky players played something else.

[Rating: 1/10] The absolute worst game I have ever played.  Funny cards do not compensate for a virtually random, pointless experience.  I actually won the game I played and still feel this way!

[Rating: 1/10] Not very fun unless you like a game with no strategy, all luck, and no rules...just bad!

[Rating: 1/10] The idea is great but the game is almost pure luck with tons of tedium and indefinite playing time... Fluxx Suxx.

[Rating: 1/10] Worthless.  Not a game.  Your decisions have very little impact on whether you win or lose.  Waste of time.  Not even remotely entertaining.

[Rating: 1/10] How to be unpopular:  Be the person who always wants to play Fluxx.  How to be even more unpopular:  Be the person who always plays that abominable "X+1" card.

[Rating: 1/10] People do this for fun!!!! Method of tourture or a great way to have an arguement.

[Rating: 1/10] Annoying, never-ending, empty of intelligence gunk. I don't know how a gamer could bring themselves to approve of such an atrocity.

[Rating: 1/10] I can see how people would enjoy this as an activity, but as a game I absolutely detest it.  Why? I can go on and on, as can the game--there is no telling whether it will last 5 minutes or an hour.  There are usually no meaningful choices to make on your turn, and the time between turns can be pretty significant.  The game changes so much between turns that there is no hope for planning.  Ugh!

[Rating: 1/10] I have a rare misprinted copy of this game - the "S" in the game title looks like an "Fl"...   See all other "1" ratings for my thoughts on the gameplay.

[Rating: 1/10] everytime I even think of this game I come back and lower my rating 1.  In fact, I'm just going to say 1 now and save myself some time.

[Rating: 1/10] I feel guilty rating it this low, but while Fluxx doesn't completely "defy the definition of a game" it is "clearly broken."  The game plays you, and does so very quickly.  The two plays of this game were both bad experiences and left the players annoyed despite only taking a round and a half a piece and less than 15 minutes total.

[Rating: 1/10] Played once and didn't care for it. My problem with it is the same as with similar card games (Landlord, Ed's Pants, Lunch Money). You have to know the cards really well and how they interact in order to form a good strategy for winning. And who has time for that when there are so many other games out there that need to be played? The "just start playing" aspect of it was difficult for me to get used to.  Guess I just like a little more structure and a lot less uncertainty...

[Rating: 1/10] I guess that barometer of how "hardcore" a gamer you are is how much you dislike Fluxx. I guess I'm there. Okay to play with non-gamers to show them there's a world outside Monopoly and Risk, but I can't imagine playing it any more.  Sold, traded, left in a parking lot somewhere -- I really don't remember.

[Rating: 1/10] THis game gives me a headache trying to follow it then i realize there is no strategy to it so I stop my mind from working and enter as much of a zen state as I can as I attempt to pretend that I am still playing the game. I would rather play 52 card pickup than play this zombie game. Torture!

[Rating: 1/10] Playing this game is something akin to being stuck in a small room with Louie Anderson, Gilbert Gottfried, and Jar Jar Binks.  I've heard people compare Fluxx with Nomic.  It's true that both games feature inconstant rules, but I don't buy the comparison.  In Nomic, the whole idea is that the players have complete control over the game - you can do anything you want with it and be as creative and unorthodox as you like.  In Fluxx, the players have virtually *no* control over the game.

[Rating: 1/10] Weird game, not interesting at all. Not challenging, no stategies at all, because there are constant changes. Do something better with the valuable time you have to play!

[Rating: 1/10] Everything I hate about gaming rolled into one tiny package of hatred and damnation.  Absolutely worthless, should appeal to hippies and lonely con-scum.

[Rating: 1/10] Only played once and if I don't play again, that'll be fine. Card game that just isn't my type.  Too much luck and that's saying something since I don't mind luck usually.
